assertion.statement: The actual primitive class-functional coordinate is regular at every height-one prime of Lambda other than(2), including(t) and(t+2), hence belongs to Lambda[1/2]. This regularity also holds at the unknown full-corank-one base.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive scalar Selmer complex, its actual class and own paired functional, and the integral derivative-switch complexes over each height-one DVR.
assertion.hypotheses: The starting generic kernel has rank one unless the actual class is zero; evaluation injection, characteristic-zero detection, exact local duality and actual-class determinant switch identities are supplied. Primitive integrality holds for the old local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every height-one prime different from(2), and each finite derivative list produced by the argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Known simple-zero ring instances and the unknown full-corank-one base, with the latter used only for regularity.
assertion.uniformity: No uniform numerical valuation bound at the unknown base is asserted. Finite switch termination is pointwise for the height-one test.
assertion.constants: All switch determinant factors are units; no new numerical constant or inverse localization value is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: At quadratic specialization the two signs are defined by actual conjugation, not a ring substitution. Finite and singular planes carry opposite J actions and exact symmetric hyperbolic cross pairing. Retain D0, strict torsion factors and the actual class-functional product.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At(t) and(t+2) use sign splitting and one-or-two-step descent, not nonquadratic irreducibility. Isotropy alone does not prove U=U-perp. Primitive vectors select primes but never replace the actual class. No inverse at an unused relaxed prime.
assertion.limit_order: Localize at a height-one prime; choose a primitive generic-kernel vector for detection; use actual derivative switches until dimension one; show the actual class and own functional integral there; transport unit-valued determinant comparisons back; intersect all height-one localizations.
